'''lsh''' is a [[copyleft]] implementation of the [[Secure Shell]] (SSH) [[protocol (computing)|protocol]] version 2, by the [[GNU Project]]<ref name=Lasser2000 /><ref name=Smith2005 /><ref name=GNUList /><ref name=GNUEntry /> including both [[server (computing)|server]] and [[client (computing)|client]] programs. Featuring [[Secure Remote Password protocol]] (SRP) as specified in secsh-srp<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-nisse-secsh-srp-01.html|title=Using the SRP protocol as a key exchange method in Secure Shell|first=Niels|last=Moller <nisse@lysator.liu.se>|website=tools.ietf.org|date=30 March 2001|accessdate=16 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://tools.ietf.org/id/draft-nisse-secsh-srp-01.txt |title=Archived copy |access-date=2014-02-06 |archive-date=2016-03-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303215259/http://tools.ietf.org/id/draft-nisse-secsh-srp-01.txt |url-status=dead }}</ref> besides, [[public-key authentication]]. [[Kerberos (protocol)|Kerberos]] is somewhat supported as well.{{Citation needed|date=July 2010}} Currently however for password verification only, not as a [[single sign-on]] (SSO) method.{{Citation needed|date=July 2010}}

lsh was started from scratch and predates [[OpenSSH]].<ref>{{Citation|title=Comparison of SSH servers|date=2020-05-30|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Comparison_of_SSH_servers&oldid=959749610|work=Wikipedia|language=en|access-date=2020-06-02}}</ref>

Karim Yaghmour concluded in 2003 that lsh was "not fit for use" in production [[embedded Linux]] systems, because of its dependencies upon other software packages that have a multiplicity of further dependencies. The lsh package requires the GNU MP library, [[zlib]], and liboop, the latter of which in turn requires [[GLib]], which then requires [[pkg-config]].  Yaghmour further notes that lsh suffers from [[cross-compilation]] problems that it inherits from glib. "If ... your target isn't the same architecture as your host," he states, "LSH isn't a practical choice at this time."<ref name=Yaghmour2003 />

[[Debian]] provides packages of lsh as <code>lsh-server</code>,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://packages.debian.org/search?searchon=names&keywords=lsh-server|title=Debian -- Package Search Results -- lsh-server|website=packages.debian.org|accessdate=16 January 2019}}</ref> <code>lsh-utils</code>, <code>lsh-doc</code> and <code>lsh-client</code>.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://packages.debian.org/squeeze/lsh-server|title=Debian -- Error|website=packages.debian.org|accessdate=16 January 2019}}</ref>
